Offset-free MPC estimator

Source: R/mpc.R
ctrl_mpc_estimator.Rd

Build a disturbance-augmented Kalman filter for offset-free tracking. The plant model is augmented with a constant disturbance \(d_{k+1} = d_k\) entering either the outputs (\(y = C x + D u + d\), type = "output") or the inputs (\(x_{k+1} = A x + B (u + d)\), type = "input"). With an observable augmented model and as many disturbances as measured outputs, the closed loop has zero steady-state tracking error for constant references and disturbances whenever it converges, even under model mismatch.

Usage

ctrl_mpc_estimator(mpc, type = c("output", "input"), Qn, Qd, Rn)

Arguments

mpc

A ctrl_mpc object.

type

"output" or "input" disturbance model.

Qn

Process noise covariance for the plant states.

Qd

Covariance of the disturbance random walk.

Rn

Measurement noise covariance.

Value

An object of class ctrl_mpc_estimator.

Details

At each sample the estimate \((\hat x, \hat d)\) is used to compute a steady-state target \((x_s, u_s)\) from $$\begin{pmatrix} A - I & B \\ C & D \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x_s \\ u_s \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -B_d \hat d \\ r - C_d \hat d \end{pmatrix}$$ (least squares when not square) and the MPC tracks it.

Examples

plant <- ctrl_c2d(ctrl_tf(1, c(1, 1)), 0.1)
mpc <- ctrl_mpc(plant, 10, Q = 0, Qy = 1, R = 0.01, u_min = -5, u_max = 5)
est <- ctrl_mpc_estimator(mpc, "output", Qn = 1e-4, Qd = 1e-3, Rn = 1e-4)
